title: Heterogeneous Accelerator Capacity Sweep (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet explores a scenario sweep for a heterogeneous accelerator fleet (A100, H100, and vendor NPUs) to identify order triggers, SKU mix tradeoffs, and cross-region runway given partial/early shipments and staggered lead times. Not a final plan — capture of heuristics, emergency lanes, assumptions, and quick sensitivity checks for Finance + SRE review.

High-level goals:
- Maintain >= 12 weeks of usable capacity (defined as capacity that meets SLOs) per major region (us-west, eu-west, apac-sin).
- Minimize premium spot/lease exposure while keeping N-day emergency burst path.
- Optimize SKU mix for typical chat/embedding workload (40% chat tokens, 60% embedding tokens).

Key assumptions (configurable):
- Baseline burn rate (tokens/hr -> GPU-hours) derived from telemetry: 1e9 chat tokens/day ~= 75 GPU-hours on H100-equivalent if steady; embedding bulk jobs are batched and use CPU-accelerated instances unless > 500k embeddings/day.
- H100 lead time (ordered today): nominal 14 weeks, vendor early partial shipments ~20% at week 10 possible; variance +/- 4 weeks.
- A100 legacy inventory: on-hand now but deprecating for new model classes; reorder lead time 8 weeks if still available via broker.
- Vendor NPU (alpha partner): lead time 20-30 weeks, but initial tranche can be delivered in split shipments (10/40/50). Integration risk: perf/compat unknown, treat as capacity discount factor 0.75 until validated.
- Cross-region transit buffer: 2 weeks for EU->US or US->APAC rebalancing.

Quick glossary:
- Usable capacity: capacity that can serve 99% of production traffic under normal routing (excludes units in burn-in, maintenance, or integration testing).
- Runway (weeks): on-hand usable capacity / expected weekly consumption.
- Emergency burst lane: short-term lease or cloud-burst allocation with per-hour premium.

Baseline inventory snapshot (textual table):
Region | On-hand (H100) | On-hand (A100) | On-hand (NPU-beta) | Usable%
---------------------------------------------------------------
us-west | 120 | 200 | 0 | 88%
eu-west | 48 | 80 | 0 | 85%
apac-sin | 32 | 40 | 0 | 80%
Global spare pool (in staging) | 24 H100 equiv | - | - | 60%

Procurement pipeline (current commits):
- Order O-2024-119 (H100) 200 units, vendor ETA: 2025-04-15 (14 weeks), partial ship 20% expected week 10 (2025-03-??). Purpose: replenish us-west + pool.
- Order O-2025-021 (NPU-beta) 300 units, vendor ETA: 2025-07-01 (26 weeks), staggered deliveries. Integration validation window planned 6 weeks post-first-arrival.
- Broker tranche B-LE-43 (A100 reorders) 50 units, ETA: 2025-02-28 (6 weeks), contingent on spot availability.

Scenario sweep summary (three canonical scenarios run interactively):
1) Conservative: vendor lead times + variance upper bound (+1 sigma) -> runway drops below 8 weeks in eu-west by week 9, triggers immediate broker lease for 60 H100-eq or accelerate O-2024-119 by negotiating 40 unit early ship.
2) Optimistic partial-ship: partial shipments arrive on schedule -> global spare pool replenished at week 10, preserves 12-week runway everywhere with only minimal lease reliance in apac.
3) Integration failure on NPU: first tranche fails perf (discount factor 0.4) -> required H100-eq top-up of 120 units allocated across us-west and eu-west; plan B is to convert broker pipeline to short-term leases and re-route embedding load to large-batch CPU instances.

Order trigger rules (proposed heuristics):
- Soft trigger: per-region runway <= 14 weeks -> start broker inquiry and secure soft options (non-binding) for up to 30% of shortfall.
- Firm trigger: per-region runway <= 10 weeks -> activate reserved-capacity negotiation + place purchase order for fast-ship tranche (if vendor supports).
- Emergency trigger: per-region runway <= 6 weeks -> start short-term cloud-burst for critical routes and A/B route fallbacks.

Staggered arrivals and allocation policy (draft):
- Partial shipments allocated in order: (1) replace degraded/retired units in same region, (2) fill emergency lane deficits, (3) top up global spare pool.
- Integration-qualified NPUs go through a 2-week canary (5% traffic) then 4-week ramp; until validated, count at 75% capacity for planning.

Risk matrix (short):
- Vendor delay (H100): high likelihood, moderate impact -> mitigation: increase broker soft options and negotiate contractual partial guarantees.
- NPU perf risk: medium likelihood, high impact -> mitigation: reserve more H100-eq until validation complete.
- Transit/regulatory hold-ups (APAC): low likelihood, high impact -> mitigation: pre-book transits, local buffer.

Small sensitivity table (text):
Parameter | Base | -10% | +10% | Notes
------------------------------------------------
H100 lead time (wks) | 14 | 12.6 | 15.4 | +/- affects runway linearly
Partial shipment fraction | 20% | 10% | 30% | affects spare pool timing
NPU perf factor | 0.75 | 0.6 | 0.9 | large effect on H100-equivalent gap

Quick decision points for next sync (Feb 5):
1) Do we push for accelerated early-shipment for O-2024-119? (Finance tradeoff: +6% unit premium vs 4 extra weeks runway)
2) Approve broker LOI for 80 H100-eq (short-term) as emergency lane?
3) Commit 2-week validation window on NPUs to determine 0.75 -> 0.9 capacity reclass.

Notes to self / loose thoughts:
- Consider converting some embedding-heavy customers to off-peak batch windows to reduce burst-hour consumption during transits.
- Explore small pilot of colocated A100 pools in eu-west for lower-cost, shorter lead-time replacements while H100 backfill arrives.
- Track model-serving quantization savings (could reduce H100-equivalent need by 8-12% over 12 weeks).
